title: GOV.UK confirms pet passports return from 1 March 2028 — but you cannot get one yet
body: GOV.UK has published ‘Pet animals: preparing for changes’, confirming the UK–EU summit on 20 November 2026 concluded the SPS agreement. From 1 March 2028, pet owners will be able to get a multiuse pet passport valid for EU travel instead of an animal health certificate for each trip. You cannot obtain one yet — passports cannot be used until 1 March 2028, and further details will be provided next year. Until then, an animal health certificate is still required for every UK to EU trip. The same guidance changes the non-commercial limit into Great Britain from 5 pets per person to 5 per vehicle, or 5 per foot passenger, and requires microchips implanted in the UK to carry a code showing the country where the animal was initially identified (from 1 March 2028 in Great Britain, 1 January 2028 in Northern Ireland).

source.label: GOV.UK — Pet animals: preparing for changes

title: UK–EU joint statement published: SPS agreement aims to apply from 1 March 2028 — pet passports still to come
body: The United Kingdom and the European Union published their joint statement (Consilium 16174/26) after the Brussels summit on 20 November 2026. The statement concludes the sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) agreement, which would let most animal movements between Great Britain and the EU take place without the certificates or controls currently required; the leaders aim to apply the agreement from 1 March 2028. The statement itself does not mention pet passports — the passport return comes from the UK government's SPS Explainer, which says owners will be able to get a multiuse pet passport instead of an animal health certificate for each trip. The tuition-fees negotiation is a separate agreement with a six-month deadline and is not linked to the SPS start date. Until the scheme starts, nothing changes at the border: an animal health certificate is still required for every UK to EU trip, and an EU pet passport held by a Great Britain resident is not valid for entry.

title: Chile: permanent ID now mandatory for dogs, cats and ferrets entering from 27 July 2026
body: Chile's SAG Exempt Resolution No. 3,343, published 28 April 2026 and in force from 27 July 2026 (repealing Resolution 6,508/2021, as amended by No. 5,444), makes permanent identification mandatory for dogs, cats and ferrets entering Chile: an ISO 11784/11785 microchip or a tattoo, with the number matching the international veterinary certificate (CVI). First rabies vaccination must be at least 21 days before entry; a clinical exam and internal and external antiparasitic treatment fall 5 to 30 days before the CVI is issued; the CVI is valid 10 days, extendable by 5. No rabies antibody test, no advance import permit and no quarantine are required. We have no Chile pages yet; US to Chile dog and cat pages are queued for verification.

source.label: Chile — LeyChile, Resolución 3343 EXENTA (2026), official text

title: Vietnam: new pet import circular in force from 1 January 2026 — one or two pets need no advance permit
body: Circular 01/2026/TT-BNNMT of Vietnam's Ministry of Agriculture and Environment, in force from 1 January 2026, replaces Circular 25/2016. Owners travelling with one or two dogs or cats declare the animals at the airport border quarantine post, which checks the origin health certificate and examines the animal, then issues the import quarantine certificate (Form 15a) within one working day if no sampling is needed. Three or more pets need advance approval from the Department of Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Medicine. The microchip must be implanted before the rabies vaccination. From 1 August 2026, Decree 204 fines walking a dog in public without a muzzle or leash at 1 to 2 million dong. We have no Vietnam pages yet; US to Vietnam dog and cat pages are queued for verification.

title: Philippines: rabies titer test and new Form 1 required for pet import permits from 1 January 2027
body: The Philippines’ Bureau of Animal Industry issued Memorandum Circular No. 60 on 26 October 2026: from 1 January 2027 every SPSIC import-permit application for a dog or cat needs a rabies antibody titer result of at least 0.5 IU/ml (FAVN or RFFIT, government-accredited lab) and a new Form 1 per animal; rabies becomes the only required vaccine, and pets must be at least 18 weeks old when the permit is applied for. Permits approved on or before 31 December 2026 travel under the old rules for their 60-day validity. We have built the US to Philippines dog and cat pages on the new rules.

source.label: Philippines Bureau of Animal Industry — Bringing dogs and cats to the Philippines

body: USDA reports 145 confirmed New World screwworm infestations in the US as of 18 November — 67 still active — across Texas, New Mexico and Arizona, including dogs in El Paso and Starr counties, Texas, and Cochise County, Arizona. Minnesota's Board of Animal Health has banned entry from USDA-designated active screwworm sites and now requires dogs and cats from affected states to travel on a vet certificate issued within 72 hours, with an approved screwworm treatment recorded on it, a rabies certificate emailed three days before arrival, and five days of quarantine after arrival. Our Mexico pages already carry the screwworm inspection certificate that has been required since 3 August 2026; owners travelling from Texas, New Mexico or Arizona should check the USDA dashboard in the week they travel.

source.label: Minnesota Board of Animal Health — import restrictions (press release)

title: Screwworm cases in the US jump to 139; Minnesota tightens pet entry from affected states

body: Industry trackers report that Turkey currently refuses entry and transit for dogs and cats arriving from Texas or New Mexico because of the US New World screwworm situation, and that Turkey asks every origin country for a rabies antibody (titer) result plus a 90-day wait after the blood draw, with entry only through six designated airports. We have not yet confirmed the Texas/New Mexico bar on a Turkish official source, so treat it as a signal to verify before booking — we are watching for the official text.
title: Turkey: dogs and cats from Texas and New Mexico reportedly barred over screwworm

body: The published joint statement (Consilium 16174/26, 20 November 2026) concludes the SPS agreement and aims to apply it from 1 March 2028 — but, like the draft before it, the statement does not mention pet passports. The passport return still rests only on the UK government's SPS Explainer, which promises a multiuse pet passport instead of an animal health certificate for each trip. Until the scheme starts, British residents travelling to the EU keep using an Animal Health Certificate for each trip — which is what all our GB to EU route pages describe.

source.label: EU–UK Joint Statement (Consilium 16174/26) and GOV.UK SPS Explainer

title: UK–EU joint statement published: SPS aims to apply from 1 March 2028 — pet passports still not in the text

body: Singapore's Animal & Veterinary Service states that from 1 April 2026, import clearance for pets arriving at the Changi Animal & Plant Quarantine station may only be handled by AVS-recognised pet agents. Owners still apply for the import licence and book the inspection themselves. Our four Singapore route pages now end with this step.

source.label: AVS — Changi Animal & Plant Quarantine Station

title: Singapore: from 1 April 2026 only AVS-recognised agents clear arriving pets at Changi

body: New Zealand's 2026 Import Health Standard for cats and dogs took effect on 1 July 2026 and runs alongside the previous standard until 1 April 2027, when it becomes the only one. Among the changes for Category 3 countries: the rabies antibody window is now 3 to 12 months before travel (it was 3 to 24), and an official pre-export identity check applies. Our New Zealand route pages follow the new standard.

source.label: MPI — Cats and Dogs 2026 Import Health Standard (PDF)

title: New Zealand's 2026 cat and dog import standard is in force — dual rules until 1 April 2027
